hints.content:
We want to complete $x^2\blueD{-10}x$ into a perfect square.

To do that, we should add $\left(\dfrac{\blueD{-10}}{2}\right)^2=\goldD{25}$ to it:

$x^2\blueD{-10}x+\goldD{25}=(x-5)^2$

In order to keep the expression equivalent, we add and subtract $\goldD{25}$, not forgetting the expression's constant term, $-96$:

$\begin{align}
f(x)&=x^2-10x-96
\\\\
&=x^2-10x+\goldD{25}-96-\goldD{25}
\\\\
&=(x-5)^2-96-25
\\\\
&=(x-5)^2-121
\end{align}$

In conclusion, after completing the square, the function is written as

$f(x)=(x - 5)^2 - 121$

This is equivalent to

$f(x)=(x+\blueD{-5})^2-121$
